podcast.title: Contract Non-Renewal and Independent Path (2004)
podcast.body: In 2004, their contract with Warner Music was not renewed, leading the band to transition to an independent career path. "But in 2004, their contract with Warner Music wasn't renewed, and the band went down the indie route."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Continued Touring and Collaborations
podcast.body: They continued to tour independently and sometimes collaborated on stage with Gordie Johnson of Big Sugar. "And they continued to tour both as themselves, and sometimes with Gordy Johnson a big sugar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Current Lineup and Family Responsibilities
podcast.body: Today, the band operates as a duo, with Shaun Verreault and Safwan Javed continuing to record and perform while managing their responsibilities as new fathers. "Today they're down to just two full-time members, vocalist and guitarist Sean Veralt, and drummer Daphon Javitt. They continued to record and perform, while balancing the responsibilities as new fathers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Major Label Deal and Juno Nominations
podcast.body: Wide Mouth Mason secured a significant major label deal and earned several Juno Award nominations during their career. "Wide Mouth Mason had a great run with a major label deal in a couple of June or award nominations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Opened for Major Rock Acts
podcast.body: The band gained significant exposure by touring with ZZ Top and opening for legendary rock groups AC/DC and The Rolling Stones. "They toured with is easy top. They opened for ACDC. They opened for the Rolling Stones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
